correctedState: The divergence is real but narrower than filed. `normalizeName` (packages/shared/src/agents/definitions.ts:281-283) trims and lowercases only, so `resolveAgentDefinition` (:718-731) matches the requested agent type case-insensitively — MEASURED: "CODE-REVIEWER" and " Code-Reviewer " both resolve to `code-reviewer` — but NOT separator-insensitively: "Code Reviewer" and "code_reviewer" both throw `Unknown agent`, which is exactly the example Claude's w20 page says now works. The gap is symmetric on both comparison arms (stored names are normalised by the same function at :441, and author-declared aliases at :699), and nothing upstream compensates: subagent-tool.ts passes the model's raw string through `asTask` (:101-110) and `normalizeSubagentRequest` (:122) to :512, and the parameter schema (:382, :419, :432) is a bare `{ type: 'string' }` with no enum of live agent names. The skill agent ceiling in prerequisite-manager.ts:450 has the same case-only fold, so it shares the gap rather than covering it. Consequence, stated accurately: a call is REJECTED with a retryable error listing the available agents — not a broken turn. The fix is one line reusing the pattern this repo already ships for permission modes (`agent/mode-types.ts:242`, `.replace(/[-_ ]/g, '')`, whose comment already reads "case- and separator-insensitively"), applied to `normalizeName` so it folds both stored names and requested ones; note that collapsing separators would also make `code-reviewer` and `codereviewer` collide, so the loader's duplicate-name behaviour should be checked in the same change.
